Preparation requires the exact process that owns the RUNNING profile runtime, verifies authenticated artifact bytes for one exact SupportTarget, creates a canonical recovery snapshot, reaches STOPPED and rechecks the logical canonical database before persisting PREPARED.

One unresolved/prepared update per profile is allowed. Apply additionally holds the normal profile runtime lease so another application runtime cannot mutate the same profile while package maintenance is in progress.

The prepared update binds profile identity, current/target release, exact manifest fingerprint, artifact id/hash, target fingerprint, data-root fingerprint and physical/logical creative snapshot evidence.
The consumer-safe wrapper rejects data roots that traverse symlinks/filesystem aliases at both prepare and apply, preventing the same path string from being retargeted onto different update state.
Apply re-verifies exact artifact trust and rejects before package mutation if the live creative database no longer matches the prepared logical snapshot.

INSTALLING is durable before invoking the replaceable package driver. Package receipts are bound to the exact request and successful install/rollback receipts must prove the resulting target/original release identity.
UNKNOWN or exceptional package-install outcome becomes RECOVERY_REQUIRED; blind retry and blind rollback are forbidden.
Known changed-package failure or clean post-update Headquarters validation failure compensates in the safe order: package rollback first, then exact creative-state snapshot restore.
Rollback failure/UNKNOWN or snapshot restore failure becomes RECOVERY_REQUIRED and never claims compensation success.
Successful update settles only after the real same-profile Headquarters opens, passes SQLite quick_check and foreign_key_check, and closes cleanly.

A consumer-safe wrapper handles the validation-close failure class: if updated Headquarters cannot prove it released the canonical database, automatic package/data rollback is bypassed and the durable journal becomes RECOVERY_REQUIRED while maintenance ownership remains fail-closed.
Update journal integrity covers both envelope hash and legal lifecycle/receipt semantics. Recomputing the hash around an impossible PREPARED->SUCCEEDED history does not make that state valid.
In-flight crash breadcrumbs such as INSTALLING, VALIDATING, ROLLING_BACK, RESTORING and FINALIZING are surfaced as requires_recovery=true and retry_allowed=false rather than restart permission.
